the-story-this-serves.text: An operator records one deployment and attaches later runs to it.
The story demands the same manifest bytes, the same mirror path and contents, the same node checks and refusal messages after the code is divided into owners.

The focused suite executes finite fixture cases: the manifest's keys, pretty bytes and newline, the output-reference spelling and four named refusals, the mirror's hex maps and replacement write, and the attachment path itself.
One row resolves two reference outputs and the state output in the recorded order, reading the provider's query record back.

Refusal rows observe the real named diagnostics for a differing script hash, a spent output, a scriptless output, an unreadable address, a contradicting seed, a different release, a missing state token, and the two live-state refusals only verification makes.

The mutation evidence is equally finite: before the move the six single-site mutants failed one, two, one, one, one and one rows; after the move a field swap failed eight of two hundred fifty rows, and a hash bypass failed the one named refusal.

Three branches have no focused row: the mirror's JSON parse refusal, a process-window-only mismatch, and the representative-policy pin through attach, which the devnet step exercises through verify. The out-of-range output index has no refusal row either, since this toolchain's read accepts it.

one-owner-per-record.text: Callers keep importing the facade, which re-exports exactly the surface they already used.

The manifest owner holds the values, their JSON, the paths and the output-reference spelling; the mirror owner holds persistence beside the manifest; the attach owner holds the release pins, verification and attachment.
The mirror reads its path and helpers from the manifest owner, so the mirror file's location has one definition.
Attachment reads the same manifest values plus the focused identity and lookup adapters the builders use, so a recorded address and a built address are derived the same way.

what-each-owner-holds.text: A table is shown here with three owners.
The manifest owner refuses an unreadable manifest naming the file, and a malformed output reference naming what was wrong.
The mirror owner refuses an unparsable mirror naming the file, and a value that is not hex.

The attach owner refuses a differently compiled release, a contradicting seed, a spent, scriptless or mismatched reference output, an unreadable address, a missing state token — and, for verification only, a live state whose active policy or windows disagree with the manifest.

the-boundary-the-record-cannot-carry.text: Folding means proving a key against the whole trie, so the deployment carries it as the mirror file beside the manifest.
That file is checked rather than hoped away, and the check belongs to the caller that attaches, not to the attach operation itself.
After attaching, the retained journey callers load the mirror and compare its root with the chain's, so a drifted copy fails by that comparison.
Attachment and verification stay two operations: verification reads the live state datum and refuses a mismatched policy or windows; attachment returns the resolved outputs without those checks.
A run that attaches is not thereby verified.

evidence-and-limits.text: The focused suite runs over files and a provider stub serving finite outputs.
The devnet identity step, wired as a pull-request workflow job, deploys a registry, verifies the intact manifest end to end, and observes the real refusal when the recorded policy is changed.
Whether that job counts as required is a repository ruleset setting no source change supplies; the row stays open until the pushed head executes it and the ruleset says so.

The focused rows are not a public journey and claim no mirror-root comparison; the retained journeys are covered by source-level mapping, not by the classified component build; and the identity step establishes same-release agreement, not cross-release stability.
The mirror-root comparison remains executable only in the retained journeys, so its status is a named limit rather than a green row.
